items.title: Commit a repro-first RED artifact proving both crash classes still live on current main
items.context: Must FAIL on current main (CLI 0.3.243, after B-506e merged at 4d417a0c4b) before any fix exists. B-506e already closed ONE class - a record that is null or a bare string now yields a typed RedEvidenceSchemaError - so do NOT include those as RED rows; they would pass and prove nothing. RECORD class still live, each verified by probe: {id:'corrupt'} versionless with no observedFailure, observedFailure of null or 123, and an ARRAY record (typeof [] is 'object', so classifyRedRecordSchemaSafe still returns 'v1' for it). ORDERING: malformed-FIRST-then-satisfying, so Array.prototype.some cannot short-circuit past it. ENVELOPE class, wholly untouched by the merge: records as {} or 42 (non-iterable TypeError) and records as 'x' (which iterates the string's characters and misreports 'a record must be an object'). SILENT class, which is NOT a crash and therefore needs a different assertion: a JSON root of [], 'x', null or 42 returns the raw value and reads as ABSENT evidence everywhere, and an unparseable file lets a raw SyntaxError escape - assert the observable wrong behaviour, not a throw. Drive everything through proofStoryDiagnosticInput then evaluateProofStoryDiagnostics, the pair the live enforce gates call, never the predicate in isolation.

happy.desc: The committed RED artifact runs on current main and FAILS, proving all three defect classes are live before any fix exists.

edge.desc: Rows that B-506e already closed (record is null or a bare string) are absent from the artifact, so no row passes vacuously.

adversarial.desc: Each class asserts the right shape: CRASH rows assert a bare TypeError escapes, SILENT rows assert a wrong observable value AND no throw, and the unparseable-file row asserts a RAW untyped SyntaxError escapes rather than asserting no throw.

items.title: Establish the pre-fix invariance baseline from main's existing five-scenario harness
items.context: SUPERSEDES the original plan to port a harness: packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs is now ON main (it arrived with the B-506e merge) and passes there, printing 2d584cc157e83ebb2f8396735f04d46946f0ba90d18a55d9fb2f263d706a11ec. That constant is therefore main's OWN pinned value, not a foreign import, and it must NOT be re-pinned. Run it BEFORE the fix to record that it passes on the pre-fix tree; that run is the baseline CHK-007 asserts against. Its five v1-only scenarios are empty store, satisfying record, blank-observedFailure record, foreign-acceptance-target record, and mixed store, each anchored by name so the digest cannot be silently re-pinned to a different verdict. Separately: 71c267a0a7372e9679d00b84be2e2b3480151bfa88939bddcae251aa750d95bc remains a phantom produced by no artifact (audit section 7.1) and must never be pinned.

happy.desc: red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs is run on the pre-fix tree and recorded as passing with digest 2d584cc1...

edge.desc: The recorded baseline names the exact commit it was taken at, so a later reader can tell whether it predates the fix.

adversarial.desc: The pinned constant is not edited, and the phantom digest 71c267a0... appears nowhere as a pinned value.

verificationEvidence.note: Pre-fix invariance baseline. main's own five-scenario harness was run unmodified on the pre-fix tree at commit 6d7c20bb4ba5bca0d7197c414284cbc4c56b3f02 and exited 0, printing five-scenario FULL-diagnostic sha256 = 2d584cc157e83ebb2f8396735f04d46946f0ba90d18a55d9fb2f263d706a11ec. That tree is pre-fix by inspection: packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts still reaches record.observedFailure.trim() immediately after the schema classify with no shape guard, and packages/main/src/core/red-evidence-artifact-validation.ts does not exist. The selector is the digest itself, so this evidence cannot pass unless the harness really recomputes that value. CHK-007 re-runs the same command post-fix and must observe the same digest; if it moves, the fix is wrong and the constant must NOT be re-pinned.

verificationEvidence.note: The baseline names its commit, and the naming is proven rather than asserted. The receipt pins BASELINE_COMMIT = 6d7c20bb4ba5bca0d7197c414284cbc4c56b3f02 and emits this selector only when three conditions hold together: the commit resolves; it is an ancestor-or-equal of HEAD, so it is genuinely on this story history; and its BLOB is pre-fix - at that commit the schema classify line in packages/main/src/core/proofstory.ts is IMMEDIATELY followed by the unguarded record.observedFailure.trim() dereference that CHK-005 will split apart, and packages/main/src/core/red-evidence-artifact-validation.ts (the CHK-004 validator) is absent from the tree. Because it reads the historical blob rather than the working tree, the assertion stays checkable after the fix lands, which is exactly what lets a later reader tell the baseline predates it. Condition-gating verified by negative runs: re-pinning BASELINE_COMMIT to an unresolvable sha, and to pre-B-506e main 1847b3af6d where the classify line does not yet exist, each suppress the marker while leaving the other marker intact.

Two adversarial conditions, both proven mechanically. (1) The pinned constant was not edited: red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs is byte-identical to main - it appears in neither git diff merge-base..HEAD nor git diff HEAD - and its V1_VERDICT_DIGEST equals the value on main, so no assertion around the constant was relaxed either. It is listed under scope-contract protectedFiles and this story never opened it for writing. (2) The phantom digest of audit section 7.1 appears nowhere under packages/main/src or packages/main/tests as a pinned value: the receipt READS the phantom out of the audit document that documents it, then scans both trees for it, so the receipt itself never becomes another place it is pinned - writing the literal here would have been the very mistake 7.1 exists to prevent, and would also have made the scan self-defeating. Condition-gating verified by a negative run: planting the extracted phantom into a scanned root suppresses this marker while leaving the baseline marker intact.

items.title: Run the mandatory migration scan over real story red-evidence artifacts and record the result
items.context: Decision D-7. Full validation was chosen, so 'no valid verdict moved' is an assumption until this scan proves it - and the pinned digest CANNOT detect the difference, because all five of its scenarios are well-formed. Enumerate every reachable red-evidence.json in real story directories; for each record compute (current verdict, verdict under full v1 validation). The story may merge only if the differing set is empty, or every entry is individually justified in the story record. Report the count even when zero: 'scanned N artifacts, 0 affected' is the evidence; silence is not.

happy.desc: The committed scan enumerates every reachable red-evidence artifact and reports a concrete count of records that satisfy the gate today while being schema-invalid.

edge.desc: The scan reports its result even when the affected set is empty, so 'scanned N artifacts, 0 affected' is positive evidence rather than silence.

adversarial.desc: The scan is re-runnable at merge time and does not hard-code the PLAN-phase snapshot of 105 artifacts / 144 records / 0 affected.

verificationEvidence.note: The committed scan walks the repository for every reachable red-evidence.json and, for each legacy v1 record, computes (verdict under the frozen pre-fix predicate, validity under the full v1 mandatory-field set derived from the RedEvidenceRecord interface by symbol). The marker is printed only when the enumeration actually covered a non-empty corpus and emitted the count line, so an empty or aborted run cannot match the selector.

items.title: Add fail-closed full v1 artifact validation at the read boundary with quarantine
items.context: Decisions D-1 to D-4. Precedence rule D-1 (which source of schema version wins): the FILE declares the era, the RECORD declares the exception, so a versionless record inside a v1-declared file is only CLAIMED v1 and must be validated against the v1 schema, never assumed to satisfy it. Validate the ENVELOPE before the records. Malformed entries are quarantined - records stays clean, malformed surface in a separate reported list - never thrown, never silently dropped. Mandatory v1 fields per the RedEvidenceRecord interface in core/types.ts (locate by symbol; the line range drifted). Cases that are easy to miss: a record missing only trigger / createdAt / id but otherwise complete is currently SATISFIED and is the WITNESS that full validation rather than the rejected narrow option was implemented; a prototype-inherited observedFailure (Object.create(null) and friends) must not be accepted via the prototype chain; and an ARRAY record must be rejected, since the classifier still returns 'v1' for it. Envelope rows from acceptance section 10.2.1: E5, a JSON root that is not an object ([], 'x', null, 42) currently does NOT crash - it flows through as the raw parsed value and every consumer reads it as ABSENT evidence, making a corrupt artifact indistinguishable from a missing one, which a crash-only validator would leave untouched; E6, a missing or unknown FILE-level schemaVersion must not silently degrade to v1; E7, an unparseable file currently lets a raw SyntaxError escape from readJson and must instead produce a typed error naming the path.

happy.desc: A well-formed v1 artifact loads unchanged and its gate verdict is identical to pre-fix.

edge.desc: Envelope rows E5, E6 and E7 each behave as specified: a non-object root is rejected rather than read as absent, a missing or unknown file-level schemaVersion does not degrade to v1, and an unparseable file yields a typed error naming the path instead of a raw SyntaxError.

adversarial.desc: Malformed entries are quarantined, not dropped: the rejected entry is retained and reported with index, identifying field and reason, and an envelope fault is never reported as a record fault. An array record and a prototype-inherited observedFailure are both rejected.

items.title: Extend the existing two-layer guard so the gate predicate is total on arbitrary input
items.context: Decision D-2. SUPERSEDES the earlier framing that main had no two-layer idiom to mirror: since the B-506e merge, main already classifies at the read boundary in store.ts and skips non-v1 records in the predicate. This story EXTENDS that shape rather than establishing it. The remaining hole is that the 'v1' class is RESIDUAL, not validated - classifyRedRecordSchemaSafe returns 'v1' for any object lacking a schemaVersion member without checking the legacy v1 shape, and it returns 'v1' for arrays too. So redEvidenceRecordSatisfied must never throw on arbitrary input even when a malformed record is injected directly into the diagnostic input, bypassing the read path. The audit verified observedFailure is the ONLY unguarded per-record dereference - every other check in the predicate is a truthiness test or a short-circuited read - so do not widen this into a rewrite of those checks.

happy.desc: The gate predicate returns a verdict for every well-formed input exactly as before.

edge.desc: The predicate never throws even when a malformed record is injected DIRECTLY into the diagnostic input, bypassing the read boundary entirely.

adversarial.desc: The other per-record checks are unchanged; only the missing shape guard is added, verified by diffing the predicate.

items.title: Make every readRedEvidence consumer surface corruption instead of aborting or degrading
items.context: There are TEN production call sites on current main, not the seven this story originally claimed - the B-506e merge added three more, and the count has now been wrong TWICE from a stale inventory, so re-derive it yourself before starting. Pre-existing seven: core/machine.ts, handlers/phase-gates.ts, handlers/proofstory.ts (three sites), handlers/story-review.ts (two sites). Added by the merge, verified absent at 1847b3af6d: core/red-evidence/append.ts, and TWO sites in handlers/red-evidence.ts (that file had zero such calls before the merge). Requirements: red_evidence_get must DISPLAY the corruption rather than abort; red_evidence_add reads before appending, so it must repair-by-append or refuse with an actionable message rather than making the artifact unrepairable through the CLI; the story_review advisory path, whose catch renders 'ProofStory Diagnostics (advisory only): unavailable (<message>)', must not let corruption read as 'feature not configured'; and the three merge-added consumers must be held to the same standard. Locate all of them by symbol, never by line number.

happy.desc: red_evidence_get displays the corruption instead of aborting, on a store carrying a malformed artifact.

edge.desc: red_evidence_add can still repair the artifact by appending, or refuses with an actionable message naming what is wrong; it never leaves the artifact unrepairable through the CLI.

adversarial.desc: All ten consumers are re-derived by symbol at implementation time and each renders corruption distinctly from absence; in particular the story_review advisory path does not let corruption read as 'feature not configured'.

items.title: Assert the invariance digest is unchanged post-fix and register the regressions in validate
items.context: Depends on the baseline recorded in CHK-002. Re-run packages/main/tests/red/red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs after the fix and assert it still passes with the SAME pinned digest 2d584cc157e83ebb2f8396735f04d46946f0ba90d18a55d9fb2f263d706a11ec - that is the 'no valid v1 verdict moved' proof, scoped per decision D-3 to records that are well-formed under the legacy v1 schema. If that digest moves, the fix changed a verdict it was not permitted to change; do not re-pin the constant to make it pass. Decision D-5: a blank observedFailure (empty or whitespace) is legacy-tolerated - it must keep producing UNSATISFIED with NO new diagnostic and must never be quarantined, because scenario 3 of that harness depends on exactly that report shape; this is the single sub-case where quarantine is overridden. Register the new tests in lattice.config.json validate.commands alongside the existing red-evidence smokes.

happy.desc: red-w2c-v1-verdict-invariance.mjs passes post-fix with the SAME pinned digest as the CHK-002 baseline.

edge.desc: A blank observedFailure still produces UNSATISFIED with no new diagnostic and is never quarantined, so scenario 3's report shape is unchanged.

adversarial.desc: If the digest moves, it is treated as a defect in the fix; the constant is not re-pinned to make the test pass.

items.context: Every other item cites decisions D-1 through D-8 and section numbers of docs/requirements/decisions/red-evidence-legacy-v1-record-validation-audit.md, which is NOT on main and would otherwise be a dangling reference for anyone reading this story independently, including the PLAN scope reviewer that reads the decisions directory. Recover REV 4 from commit 9583fb95aa2e5d3dda094dfc2341aa6d9e835722 (same path, retrievable from any worktree via git show) and land it in this story's diff. Do this as the LITERAL FIRST action of PLAN, before understanding_set - plan.md DependsOn only orders DEV-phase dispatch and cannot reach back into PLAN-phase timing. Read its section 0.0 FIRST: it records that sibling story B-506e has MERGED into main, which inverted an earlier provenance warning; rev 4 additionally corrects the consumer count to ten, downgrades the E5 row from a crash to a silent misread, and fixes a D-2 row that contradicted section 0.0.

happy.desc: The decision document is present at docs/requirements/decisions/ in the story diff and its D-1..D-8 citations resolve.

edge.desc: It is landed before the PLAN scope review runs, not at the end of the story.

adversarial.desc: The landed copy has no header text contradicting its own section 0.0 about which tree the citations describe.

verificationEvidence.note: Tool-executed receipt: the marker prints only if the decision record is BOTH present in commit b8c458422e (this story's diff) AND actually contains the D-8 decision row, so the citations threaded through the other ten items resolve for an independent reader.

Tool-executed ORDERING receipt rather than an assertion: git rev-list --ancestry-path yields the first scope_check_save commit only if the doc commit is genuinely its ancestor. Had the doc landed after the PLAN scope review the output would be empty and the selector could not match.

Tool-executed receipt that the stale pre-merge header was rewritten rather than merely supplemented: it prints only if the corrected wording is present AND the old self-contradicting line is absent. A negative control (mutating the condition) was run and confirmed the marker disappears, so the receipt is not vacuous.

items.title: Prove the gate verdict is order-independent after the fix
items.context: Added in PLAN per INIT-002 / DRAFT-106, raised twice by the INIT reviewer and re-verified live on current main. Decision document acceptance section 10.3 requires BOTH ordering rows, and only O1 was covered. O1, malformed entry first, crashes today and is a CHK-001 repro row. O2, a satisfying record FIRST and a malformed entry after, does NOT crash: redEvidenceSatisfied uses Array.prototype.some, which short-circuits on the first satisfying record, so the malformed entry is never examined and the gate returns SATISFIED while the artifact is corrupt. That makes the outcome depend on array position, which is a defect in its own right and cannot be caught by a crash-only test. After the fix, assert that the SAME record set produces the SAME verdict regardless of position, and that a malformed entry is reported even when a satisfying record precedes it.

happy.desc: After the fix, the same record set produces the same verdict regardless of the position of the malformed entry.

edge.desc: A malformed entry is reported even when a satisfying record precedes it, so Array.prototype.some short-circuiting can no longer hide it.

adversarial.desc: The pre-fix behaviour is pinned first: satisfying-first-then-malformed returns SATISFIED today with no throw, proving the assertion is not vacuous.

items.title: Assert the behaviour this fix must NOT change
items.context: Closes two scope gaps found by the PLAN scope reviewer (decision document acceptance rows V2 and E4), neither of which was owned by any item. V2: a valid v2 record must remain unchanged and continue to be correctly skipped by the v1 predicate - the v2 record union arrived on main with the B-506e merge, so this is live behaviour that a read-boundary validator could easily break by rejecting records it does not recognise. E4: an artifact whose records key is ABSENT must keep producing UNSATISFIED, which is the ordinary not-configured path and must NOT be reclassified as corruption; conflating absent with malformed would regress the very distinction this story exists to create. Both are regression assertions against behaviour that is correct today, not new capability.

happy.desc: A valid v2 record is still correctly skipped by the v1 predicate and its handling is unchanged from pre-fix.

edge.desc: An artifact whose records key is ABSENT still produces UNSATISFIED via the ordinary not-configured path and is NOT reclassified as corruption.

adversarial.desc: Absent and malformed remain distinguishable end to end: an absent artifact reports as not configured while a corrupt one reports as corrupt, at every consumer.

items.title: Fuzz the validator to prove it is total on arbitrary JSON
items.context: Closes the third scope gap: decision document section 10.5 requires that the validator ITSELF cannot throw on any JSON shape, and the checklist only pinned the specific enumerated malformed and envelope rows. Those rows were written from observed failures, so they prove the known cases and nothing about the unknown ones - which is the same mistake, in test form, that produced this defect in the first place. Generate arbitrary acyclic JSON values (nested objects and arrays, mixed primitives, empty containers, deeply nested structures, and objects with no prototype) and assert the validator returns a classification for every one of them and never throws. This is a property, not a case list.

happy.desc: The validator returns a classification for arbitrary acyclic JSON values and never throws.

edge.desc: Coverage includes empty containers, deeply nested structures, mixed primitive arrays, and objects created with no prototype.

adversarial.desc: The property is asserted over generated inputs rather than the enumerated failure rows, so it can catch shapes nobody thought to list - the same blind spot that produced this defect.

auditLog.reason: INIT reviewer raised this twice (DRAFT-106 then INIT-002) and it was deferred to PLAN on the explicit condition that it become a real checklist item rather than an optional addition; acceptance section 10.3 row O2 was otherwise covered by no item.
